status: design decisions fixed (user 2026-10-08: 'go ahead with your recommendations for p 2'); stage P2-0 frozen below; the scene generator and panels are frozen in a later amendment before any Phase-2 scene data is generated
question: Does the image-only fork monitor (DINOv2 latent -> learned dynamics -> 64 futures -> goal-free split test) catch forks on scene TYPES it was never trained on, with an uncertainty model that knows nothing about the objects?
why: The task-agnostic claim has only been tested on one scene (three upright blocks, pick the middle one). The G operator injects perception error as pose noise on exactly three named blocks, which cannot exist for an arbitrary scene.

scenes.generator: procedural MJCF scenes on the existing Panda table (vendor/panda_express_sim): 2-6 free objects; shapes box / cylinder / slab with sampled sizes, masses, friction; random layouts with a reachable target

families.F1_rows: rows of upright objects with gaps 0-15 mm (generalises the 3-block task)
families.F2_stacks: 2-3 object stacks, target on top or at the bottom
families.F3_leaning: one object leaning on another or on a wall
families.F4_clutter: loose clutter, objects touching at random

scenes.actions: scripted pick and push primitives toward the target (approach, descend, grasp/push, lift/hold) with randomised offsets, so each chunk start has a nominal 8-step chunk; bench execution-noise snippets as now
scenes.OPEN_1: which families to build first (proposal: F1 + F2 for training, F3 held out; F4 later)

fork_label_for_grading_only: generic harm event in 2-62 of 64 oracle futures: any NON-target object tilts >= 45 deg, falls off the table, or moves >= 30 mm (OPEN_2: thresholds). Oracle futures from the true state + perception draws on every object's pose + execution snippets, as now.

object_free_uncertainty.problem: G(z0, d) needs d = per-block pose noise for 3 known blocks
object_free_uncertainty.proposal: G* : (z0, eps) -> perturbed start latent, eps ~ N(0, I) of fixed size, trained on (true-state latent, rendered perturbed-start latent) pairs with an energy-score / set loss so that its 64 samples match the spread of 64 real perturbed renders; at run time only the image latent and noise go in (no object count, poses or names). Perception error during training data generation is still applied per object in the simulator (that is how the real spread is produced).
object_free_uncertainty.check: on the 3-block task, G* in place of G must keep US within 0.03 of its H score before Phase 2 uses it (a separate pre-test, P2-0)
object_free_uncertainty.OPEN_3: alternative: noise directly in latent space scaled by measured per-location latent error (cheaper, cruder)

training: Phase-1e US recipe (deterministic conv step model, label-free rare-mode rebalancing) with label-free curation from Phase 1f if it passed; same latent (DINOv2 ViT-S/14 392 -> channel PCA 8, PCA refit on the training families only)

evaluation.in_family: fresh panels from the training families with unseen parameters
evaluation.held_out_family: panel from the held-out family (never used for training, PCA fitting or selection)
evaluation.references: MuJoCo exact-start probe (oracle state), second oracle run, always-stay / always-alarm baselines, and the 3-block-only US model (to show what training diversity adds)
evaluation.metrics: forks caught and false alarms (R0, R1), per family

gates: OPEN_4 (proposal): held-out family >= 70% caught with <= 20% false alarms, and in-family >= 80% / <= 20%
stages_and_cost: P2-0: G* on the 3-block task (training G* ~2 h GPU, US evaluation ~0.5 h)
scene generator + scripted primitives + harm label (engineering, ~1-2 days)
screen, select (label-free as Phase 1f) and render training data for 2 families (~1-2 days CPU)
panels: in-family and held-out (~0.5 day CPU)
out_of_scope: real images; V-JEPA 2-AC (separate protocol, can use the GPU while Phase 2 data generates on the CPU)

decisions.OPEN_1_families: train on F1 rows + F2 stacks; F3 leaning is the held-out family; F4 clutter later
decisions.OPEN_2_harm_thresholds: non-target object tilt >= 45 deg, falls off the table, or moves >= 30 mm
decisions.OPEN_3_uncertainty: learned object-free sampler G* (recommended); the cheaper latent-noise sampler is kept as a pre-declared comparator in P2-0 because the step3b P1 check (results/jenga/step3b_p1_result.json) found a global latent-PCA Gaussian sampler on par with G
decisions.OPEN_4_gates: held-out family >= 70% caught with <= 20% false alarms; in-family >= 80% / <= 20% (R0)

P2_0.status: frozen before execution (2026-10-08), before any G* training
P2_0.question: Can the 3-block G operator (18-number pose noise on named blocks) be replaced by an object-free start sampler without losing US's H accuracy?

samplers.Gstar: PerturbNet body (as G: 4 FiLM blocks, width 96) with its 18-number pose input replaced by eps ~ N(0, I_32); trained on the Phase-1 enriched training states (z0 -> rendered perturbed starts z0k) with the energy score per state: 8 G* samples vs 8 of the state's real z0k (random subset), ES = mean||X-Y|| - 0.5 mean||X-X'|| on flattened latents; batch 16 states, 8,000 steps, AdamW 1e-3 cosine, weight decay 1e-4, seed 0
samplers.Gauss: z0 + mean + top-64 principal directions of (z0k - z0) over the same training states with their measured standard deviations (eval/step3b_models.fit_gaussian refit on the enriched data); no network

P2_0.step_B: only if neither passes A: retrain US (fast recipe, seed 0) with the sampler replacing G in the 50/50 start mix, evaluate as A, same pass rule

P2_0b_start_sampler_for_varied_layouts.why: P2-0 selected Gauss (score 0.709 vs G 0.672), but its 64 noise directions span the whole 28x28 grid and were fit where the three blocks sit in the 3-block camera view; they cannot move with objects in new layouts

candidates.Gauss_TE: translation-equivariant: zero-mean stationary Gaussian field on the 28x28x8 grid; per-location 8x8 channel covariance and spatial correlation (radially averaged over lags 0-4 cells) estimated from (z0k - z0) on the training states; sampled by convolving white noise with the fitted kernel
candidates.Gauss_TE_masked: Gauss_TE with each location's amplitude scaled by a background score: a(x) = clip((||z0(x) - m|| - q5) / (q95 - q5), 0, 1), where m is the median latent over all locations of all training images and q5/q95 are percentiles of ||z0 - m|| over the same; noise concentrates where the image differs from plain table. No object detection, count or pose

P2_0b_start_sampler_for_varied_layouts.test: as P2-0 step A on H with the Phase-1e US model (evaluation-only swap, own floor); pass = within 0.03 of US with G (0.672)
P2_0b_start_sampler_for_varied_layouts.use: the best passing location-independent candidate (Gauss_TE or Gauss_TE_masked) becomes the Phase-2 sampler, refit on Phase-2 training families. If neither passes, Phase 2 proceeds with Gauss_TE_masked and reports the 3-block shortfall (no further sampler search)
P2_0b_start_sampler_for_varied_layouts.run_when: after Phase-1f screening frees the GPU (single process, minutes)

simulator.base: the existing Panda scene (vendor/panda_express_sim panda_jenga_setup.xml): same robot, table, controller (DirectJengaSim execute/_control), 0.1 s control step, physics options
simulator.scene_builder: eval/phase2_scenes.py writes one MJCF per scene from a seed: the three named blocks are replaced by N free bodies obj0..objN-1 (obj0 = target); all objects must lie inside the close-camera view (lookat 0.5, 0, 0.46; distance 0.30) with >= 60% of each object's pixels visible in the true-start render (checked by segmentation render; scenes failing it are re-drawn with the next seed)
simulator.objects: shape box / cylinder / slab; box half-sizes x 8-16 mm, y 8-14 mm, z 20-45 mm; cylinder radius 8-14 mm, half-height 20-45 mm; slab half-sizes 25-40 x 12-18 x 5-8 mm; mass 25-120 g; sliding friction 0.5-1.0 (MuJoCo default torsional/rolling); colours drawn per object from a fixed 8-colour palette (the target is NOT always red)
simulator.settling: after building, 1.0 s of physics with the robot at its home pose; scenes in which any object moves > 5 mm or tilts > 5 deg during settling (unstable by construction) are re-drawn, EXCEPT F3 where the leaning contact must persist (re-drawn if it slips > 5 mm)

families.F1_rows: 2-5 upright boxes or cylinders in a row along y, gaps 0-15 mm, row yaw +-10 deg, small per-object yaw/position jitter as the 3-block reset (+-2 mm, +-3 deg); target = a random object of the row
families.F2_stacks: 1-2 stacks of 2-3 objects (box or slab bases, box/cylinder/slab on top, offset 0-8 mm), plus 0-2 upright neighbours within 0-20 mm; target = a top object (pick) or a stack/neighbour object (push)
families.F3_leaning_HELD_OUT: one object leaning 10-30 deg on an upright neighbour or on a fixed low wall, plus 0-2 further neighbours; target = leaning, supporting or neighbouring object. Never used for training, PCA, sampler fitting, selection or tuning

actions.format: 4-D commands (xyz target, gripper +1 close / -1 open) at 10 Hz, as the Jenga replays
actions.primitives: PICK: move above target (approach height 60-120 mm), descend to grasp height, close, lift 80 mm; PUSH: move to a pre-push point 20-40 mm behind the target on a random horizontal direction, lower, push 30-80 mm through the target, retract. Waypoints interpolated at 5-12 mm per step (sampled speed)
actions.randomisation: grasp/push offset +-12 mm, approach yaw of the push direction +-25 deg, descent depth +-8 mm; these make some chunks brush or bump neighbours, which is where forks come from
actions.episodes: one primitive per scene (PICK or PUSH, family-dependent), 40-90 commands; chunk starts every 8 commands (chunk_starts), oracle/latent futures as now (8-command chunk + 30-step hold on the last target)

amendment_8.predictor: spatial transformer step model replacing the conv net, same interface and recipe: the 28x28x8 latent is patchified 2x2 -> 196 tokens (dim 32 -> 384) + learned 2-D position embeddings + 4 register tokens; 6 blocks, width 384, 6 heads, MLP 4x, AdaLN-Zero conditioning on the embedded action pair (after Toso et al. 2026 and WorldDiT); attention across all locations; output: per-token linear -> 2x2x8 residual (unpatchified). Deterministic, unrolled 19 steps as the US recipe

arms.T: transformer predictor, US2_long recipe otherwise (label-free rare-mode rebalancing, 50/50 Gauss-TE or rendered starts, input noise, hold weights, 22,500 steps at batch 128, lr x2 cosine, seed 0)
arms.T_pix: T plus an auxiliary head (training only; absent at inference) predicting per-patch-normalised RGB of the REAL future close-camera frame at hold 10 and hold 30: frame downsampled to 112x112, 14x14 patches of 8x8x3 = 192 values each normalised by its own mean and std (as WorldDiT); head = linear from the 196 output tokens; loss weight 0.01 (MSE), applied at model steps HOLD10 and HOLD30

amendment_8.data: the existing 4,800 Phase-2 training states; future frames re-rendered with the identical seeds and future order as eval/phase2_data.py and verified against the stored traces (max abs difference < 1e-6 required, else the arm is not run)
amendment_8.grading: H2 with the BOTH readout and each model's own floor, beside US2_long seeds 0/1 (0.188 / 0.276) and US2_xlong (0.266); 'transformer helps' if T or T_pix scores > 0.276 + 0.05; amendment-5 rule for panels (>= 80% / <= 20% on H2)
amendment_8.compute: T on the 3090, T_pix on the 5080 (frames copied over), in parallel

amendment_9.status: frozen before any code runs (user: 'sure build and run the set-level objective')
amendment_9.basis: amendment 8: transformers reach the lowest training loss (0.039) yet do not branch better (T 0.06, T_pix 0.19 vs conv 0.19-0.28); per-family breakdown shows a uniform ~half-of-ceiling gap. Per-future regression from paired starts smears across forks; sampled (Gauss-TE) starts used by the monitor never receive a direct training signal
amendment_9.set_loss: each step, S = 8 training states (4 drawn uniformly from states whose own futures have a rare mode -- label-free -- and 4 uniformly from all states); for each, M = 8 of its real futures (uniform without replacement) give the real set Y (hold-10 and hold-30 latents) and their executed actions; the model is rolled 19 steps from 8 Gauss-TE starts (one per real future's actions) giving X. Set term = energy distance per state: mean||X-Y|| - 0.5 mean_{i!=j}||X_i-X_j|| - 0.5 mean_{i!=j}||Y_i-Y_j||, divided by sqrt(D), averaged over hold 10 and hold 30 and the S states
amendment_9.objective: per-future US recipe loss (unchanged batch of 128) + lambda * set term

arms.SL_low: lambda such that lambda x (initial set term) = 0.5 x (initial per-future loss)
arms.SL_high: lambda such that lambda x (initial set term) = 5 x (initial per-future loss)

amendment_9.calibration: initial values measured on 20 training batches with the starting model before any update (seed 0); recorded in the result
amendment_9.training: all arms fine-tune US2_long (seed 0, the 0.188 model) for 7,500 steps at batch 128, AdamW lr 1.5e-4 (fast recipe lr / 4) cosine, seed 0, same rare-mode rebalancing, Gauss-TE / rendered start mix, input noise and hold weights
amendment_9.grading: H2 with BOTH and own floor; 'set loss helps' if the better SL arm scores >= C0 + 0.10 (above the observed seed spread 0.09); panels only under the amendment-5 rule (>= 80% / <= 20% on H2)
amendment_9.compute: C0 on the 3090, SL_low then SL_high on the 5080
